fullstack.title: Full-stack engineer (Next.js / Node)
fullstack.summary: You will build and run the web apps, portals and APIs our clients use every day, from the first sketch to production support.
do: Build features across the stack in TypeScript, Next.js and Node
Design data models and APIs with the rest of the team
Ship to production, monitor and fix what breaks
Talk to clients to understand the problem behind a request
bring: Two or more years building web applications
Solid TypeScript or JavaScript, SQL and Git
Care for the details users notice
Clear written French or English; Kinyarwanda is a plus

technician.title: Field technician (hardware & networks)
technician.summary: You will install, maintain and repair the devices and networks our clients rely on, in Kigali and across the country.
do: Install and configure computers, printers and network equipment
Diagnose and repair hardware on site and in the workshop
Run preventive maintenance visits for contract clients
Document every intervention in the help desk
bring: Experience with hardware repair and basic networking
A methodical way of working and a calm manner with clients
Willingness to travel for on-site visits
A driving licence is a plus

items.q: What does a support contract cover?
items.a: The systems, software and devices listed in your contract: help desk access, the response times above, preventive maintenance and on-site visits where included.

items.q: How do I open a ticket?
items.a: Email the help desk or call us during support hours. Give your company name, what happened and how urgent it is; you get a ticket number in reply.

items.q: Do you support hardware you did not supply?
items.a: Often, yes. We first check the device and tell you what we can support and at what cost before any work starts.

items.q: Can you come on site outside Kigali?
items.a: Yes, nationwide. Visits outside Kigali are scheduled with you in advance; travel is quoted separately unless your contract includes it.
A session only starts when you give the code shown on your screen, you see everything the technician does, and you can end it at any time.

meta.title: Privacy policy
meta.description: How Linsetech Ltd collects, uses, stores and protects personal data, your rights under Rwanda's data protection law, and the cookies this site uses.

intro.heading: Your privacy matters to us.
body: This policy explains what personal data Linsetech Ltd (“Linse”, “we”) collects through this website and when you contact us, why we use it, who receives it, how long we keep it and the rights you have under Law No 058/2021 of 13/10/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy in Rwanda.
Last updated: 10 November 2026. Questions about this policy or your data can be sent to {email}.

sections.title: Who we are
body: Linsetech Ltd is a company registered in Rwanda, based in Kigali. We design and build software, publish our own products, supply business hardware and provide IT services.
For the personal data described here, Linsetech Ltd is the data controller: we decide why and how it is used. You can reach us at {email}.

sections.title: What we collect
body: What you send us. When you use the contact or project form: your name, email address, company (optional), the kind of help you need and your message. When you apply for a job: your name, email address, the role and a link to your CV or portfolio. When you join our newsletter: your email address and, if you choose, your first and last name, company and topics.
When we work together. Contact details of the people we deal with, and the information needed to quote, deliver, invoice and support our services and products.

Technical data. Our hosting provider records basic technical information when you visit (such as your IP address, browser type and the pages requested) to deliver the site and keep it secure. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies.

sections.title: How we use it, and why
body: To answer your enquiry and prepare a quote or proposal: this is necessary to take steps at your request before a contract.
To deliver, invoice and support what you buy from us: this is necessary to perform our contract with you or your organisation.
To consider your job application: necessary to take steps at your request; we use your data only for recruitment.
To send our newsletter: based on your consent, which you can withdraw at any time with the unsubscribe link or by writing to us.
To run, secure and improve this website, and to keep business records: our legitimate interests, and our legal obligations (for example tax and accounting rules).
We do not sell personal data, and we do not make decisions about you based solely on automated processing.

sections.title: Who receives it
body: Our team, on a need-to-know basis.

Service providers who process data for us under contract and only on our instructions: our website host (Vercel Inc.), our email provider, which delivers form messages to our inbox, and, if you join it, our newsletter service.
Authorities, courts or advisers, when the law requires it or to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

sections.title: Storage outside Rwanda
body: Some of our providers, including our website host, store or process data outside Rwanda. The law requires personal data to be stored in Rwanda unless storage abroad is authorised by the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA).
We store and transfer personal data outside Rwanda only as the law allows, with appropriate safeguards in place with each provider. Ask us at {email} for details of where your data is held.

sections.title: How long we keep it
body: Enquiries and proposals that don't lead to work: 24 months after our last exchange.
Client and contract records: for the duration of the contract and as long as tax, accounting and other legal obligations require afterwards.
Job applications: 12 months after the role is filled, unless you agree to a longer period.
Newsletter: until you unsubscribe.
Hosting logs: kept by our host for a short period for security, typically no more than 30 days.
When data is no longer needed, we delete or anonymise it.

sections.title: Security
body: The website is served over an encrypted connection (HTTPS). Access to personal data is limited to the people who need it, accounts are protected, and we choose providers that apply recognised security measures.
No system is completely secure. If a breach affecting your personal data occurs, we will act on it and notify the NCSA and, where required, the people affected, as the law requires.

sections.title: Your rights
body: Under Rwanda's data protection law you have the right to be informed about how your data is used; to access your data and get a copy of it; to have inaccurate data corrected; to have data erased when it is no longer needed or was processed unlawfully; to object to processing, including for direct marketing; to restrict processing; to data portability; and not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing.
Where we rely on your consent, you can withdraw it at any time; this does not affect what was done before.
To exercise any of these rights, write to {email}. We may ask you to confirm your identity, and we will reply within the time the law sets.
If you are not satisfied with our answer, you can lodge a complaint with the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA), Rwanda's data protection authority.

sections.title: Cookies
body: This site uses only the cookies it needs to work. We don't use advertising or tracking cookies, and if we add website statistics they will be cookie-free.
linse_cookie_consent: remembers that you have seen and closed the cookie notice, so it isn't shown again. Kept for 1 year.
NEXT_LOCALE: remembers the language you are browsing in (English, French or Kinyarwanda). Kept until you close your browser.
You can delete or block cookies in your browser settings; the site will still work, but the notice may appear again and the language may reset.

sections.title: Children
body: This website and our services are meant for businesses and adults. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 16. If you believe a child has sent us personal data, contact us and we will delete it.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
body: We may update this policy when our services or the law change. The date at the top shows the latest version; important changes will be highlighted on this page.

Articles and guides, including those on tax, payments or data protection, are not legal, tax or financial advice: check your own situation with a qualified adviser or the relevant authority.

Our services, products, hardware sales and support are governed by the agreement, order or terms we provide for them, which take precedence over these terms.

sections.title: Intellectual property

You may use the files in our logo pack to refer to Linse, following the brand guidelines on this site. Any other use of our content or marks needs our written permission.

sections.title: What you send us
body: When you send us information through a form or by email, you confirm it is accurate and that you are entitled to share it. Please don't send confidential information or passwords through the website forms.
We use personal data as described in our Privacy policy.

sections.title: Third-party links

sections.title: Liability

Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited under Rwandan law.
